title: Papyrus relevance through Cyclotron in shadow mode
description:
## Goal (Papyrus repo, with the Cyclotron repo; tracked here as part of the review follow-through)
Route Papyrus source relevance through Cyclotron in shadow mode and measure it before relying on it.

## Plan
1. Papyrus opens a `papyrus-relevance` cyclotron as shown in Cyclotron `docs/embedding.md` (single classifier: "Should this source become a reference for this publication?", positive label include). Seed the rubric from the publication doctrine. Use an exclusive Assignment claim as the single-writer lease.
2. For each reference, Biblicus supplies extracted text and web metadata (that is the application transformer Cyclotron expects). The Cyclotron decision is recorded next to the current 1 to 5 quality rubric in `reference_curation_signals.py`. It does not change any editorial outcome.
3. Editor accept or reject becomes a review (`cyclotron.review`).
4. After enough real reviews, compare Cyclotron's accuracy and calibration with the rubric on the same items. Promote only if it wins; record the numbers.
5. Then repeat for steering proposal acceptance.

## Done when
Shadow decisions are recorded for every new reference and a written comparison on real editor labels exists.

comments.author: home
comments.text: 2026-10-19 audit of Papyrus origin/main (a35694b5). Done: step 1 (papyrus-relevance cyclotron seeded from doctrine, AssignmentClaimLease in relevance_sweep.py), step 3 (editor accept/reject -> cyclotron.review, relevance_sweep.py:598), shadow recording with live agreement (relevance_shadow.py, PR 298/304). Not done: (a) no comparison of Cyclotron against the 1-5 quality rubric (reference_curation_signals.py:64 QUALITY_ASSESSMENT_RUBRIC still present and feeds ranking); the only proof is lib/approved-priming-proofs/papyrus.json, 10 held-out sources, agreement 0.9 at 13 labels, no calibration values, no rubric baseline. (b) step 5, steering proposal acceptance through Cyclotron: nothing exists. Remaining work: pair each shadow decision with quality_rating_is on the same reviewed References, n well above 10, record accuracy and calibration for both, then decide promotion. Then step 5. Opt-in auto-reject of clear misses (PR 358) already gates on a fresh proof.

comments.author: home
comments.text: 2026-10-21 status from the Cyclotron session: no paired evidence exists at any n. The only live relevance cyclotron (p.apyr.us, set up 2026-10-20) has made 0 shadow decisions: its corpus knowledge-corpus-p-apyr-us has no pending references and it holds 1 primed example. The legacy Papyrus steering store pointed at the Threat Intelligence bucket, where no store exists. Next step is an offline backtest: replay editor-reviewed References that have both an accept/reject outcome and a rubric quality_rating_is through a fresh cyclotron on a held-out split; report accuracy against the editor decision for the cyclotron and for the rubric at its current cut-off, calibration (Brier score and reliability bins), and the disagreement cases. Cost: roughly 100-300 paid decision-model requests on production data; waiting for Ryan's go-ahead and budget (the Cyclotron session asked). Open question: which corpus has the most reviewed References with quality_rating_is (Papyrus data). blbs-ca6f88 stays blocked on this.

comments.author: home
comments.text: 2026-10-21 count by the Cyclotron session (read-only; sites p.apyr.us, threat-intelligence and anth-us, pilobol only partly checked): the rubric-vs-Cyclotron comparison cannot be measured on current data. (1) 0 quality_rating_is SemanticRelations exist in production, current or superseded. (2) Papyrus never stores ratings 1 or 2: setReferenceQualityRating (amplify/functions/category-action/handler.ts around 555-566) writes the relation only when rating >= 3 and rejects otherwise, so the cut-off is accept iff >= 3 and low ratings are lost. (3) No rejection reason codes are recorded (2 comment relations in total, both accepts, reasonCode null). (4) The largest labelled set, p.apyr.us knowledge-corpus-ai-ml-research, has 1,376 accepted and 20 rejected, but 1,341 accepts are bulk trusted imports and 15 rejects are housekeeping; only 6 references were human-reviewed. Threat-intelligence's 25 labels come from an E2E agent. No paid backtest was run. Options: (a) an editor rates a spread of a few hundred pending ai-ml-research references (4,618 pending) and Papyrus stores ratings 1 and 2; or (b) redefine this issue's target as accept/reject only, which still needs a few hundred human editor decisions. Decision is Ryan's.
